q: A teacher wants to organize documents, slides, and spreadsheets for one unit. What is the best first step?
choices: Create a Drive folder for the unit
exp: A dedicated Drive folder creates a clear structure.

q: Form responses need to be sorted, filtered, and charted. Where should the teacher work with the data?
exp: Sheets supports sorting, filtering, formulas, and charts.

q: Which two actions are useful when reviewing Form results in Sheets? (Select two.)
choices: Start a Meet call to change formulas
exp: Sorting/filtering and charts are common data-analysis tasks.

q: You need a quick visual summary of survey responses by category. What should you create in Sheets?
exp: Charts provide visual summaries of data.

q: A spreadsheet of student names should be alphabetized while keeping all row data together. What should you do?
choices: Sort the full data range by the name column
exp: Sorting the full range preserves row relationships.

q: Which Gmail feature is most useful for automatically applying a 'Parents' label to messages from a known sender?
exp: A filter can detect sender criteria and apply a label automatically.

q: You want to quickly find a Drive file when you remember part of its name. What is the best first action?
exp: Drive search is designed for fast retrieval.

q: Which naming practice makes files easier to manage over time?
exp: Consistent descriptive names improve retrieval and organization.

q: A teacher wants to keep frequently used curriculum files together without duplicating them unnecessarily. Which approach is sensible?
choices: Use organized Drive folders and shortcuts where appropriate
Create ten copies of every file
Put everything in one unsorted folder
exp: Folders and shortcuts reduce duplication while improving access.

q: Which two strategies improve Gmail retrieval? (Select two.)
choices: Delete the subject from every message
exp: Labels and search operators make large inboxes easier to manage.

q: A teacher wants to display only rows where the class is '5A' without deleting other rows. Which Sheets feature is appropriate?
exp: Filters temporarily show only rows that meet selected criteria.

q: A teacher has response data with a header row. What should be included when sorting the data?
choices: The full table range, with the header recognized appropriately
Only one cell in the middle
exp: Sorting should preserve full rows and respect the header.

q: You need to calculate the average of numeric ratings in a Sheet. Which approach is best?
choices: Use an AVERAGE formula on the rating range
exp: The AVERAGE function calculates the mean of a numeric range.

q: A Drive folder is becoming difficult to navigate. Which two actions would help? (Select two.)
choices: Move everything into one unnamed folder
Make duplicate copies of every file
exp: Subfolders and consistent names improve navigability.

q: Which search is best for finding messages from 'admin@school.org' with a PDF attachment?
exp: Gmail search operators can combine sender, attachment, and filename criteria.

q: A teacher wants to compare category counts in a Sheet. Which visualization is often appropriate for discrete categories?
exp: Bar or column charts are commonly useful for comparing category counts.
